headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to reduce residential energy costs by requiring large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for their own dedicated grid infrastructure and capacity.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor's administration
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: This bill proposes to make data centers shoulder more energy costs, potentially saving residential ratepayers over $65 annually. It requires data centers to pay for their own electrical substations and capacity costs, aiming to reduce the burden on other customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandate
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency regarding the industry's water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales to data centers, separating potable and non-potable withdrawals. This legislation, sponsored by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to increase transparency and provide crucial data for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data centers, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: This new law, effective July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise impacts on nearby homes and schools. While it mandates studies and disclosures, it does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks, leaving some discretion to localities.
